author.name: Efficiency Emilia
author.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.

challenge.name: The Silent Store Gap
challenge.description: A batch of till scan lines from the northern stores was silently dropped during last night's ingestion, causing the model to forecast zero demand for fresh produce. #reliability_ruth# argues that the ingestion pipeline must be fully automated to guarantee every store's data arrives on time, while #data_dave# is willing to accept a manual verification step to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store.

output.content: The current feature store architecture is too heavy for our operational budget. We are spending too much on maintenance and infrastructure for the northern stores alone. I am willing to accept a simpler, less flexible feature store if it cuts those ongoing costs significantly. We do not need every possible historical attribute if the system becomes harder to run. Let us strip out the complex transformations that add little value to the replenishment logic. A leaner setup that keeps the core scan lines and stock levels clean is worth more to us than a sprawling repository that drains the team. We can live with reduced analytical depth to keep the platform affordable and reliable for the daily forecast job.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states a willingness to accept a simpler, less flexible feature store and reduced analytical depth in exchange for significantly lower ongoing costs and higher reliability.
